title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, as companies scramble to secure funding and partnerships while governments bolster defense budgets. Notably, India’s Jio is laying the groundwork for a sovereign LEO constellation, while Northrop Grumman is keen on ramping up solid rocket production.

themes.title: India's LEO Ambitions
themes.body: India's Jio is making headlines with its plans for a sovereign LEO constellation, aiming to capitalize on the growing demand for satellite services. This move comes just ahead of its IPO, suggesting a strategic play to attract investors with a forward-looking vision.

themes.title: Consolidation in Space Tech
themes.body: MDA Space's acquisition of Blue Canyon Technologies signals a trend of consolidation as companies seek to strengthen their foothold in the competitive U.S. market. As the landscape evolves, expect more such deals as firms aim to enhance capabilities and market share.

themes.title: Funding Rounds Galore
themes.body: ElevationSpace's recent $40 million Series B funding round exemplifies the ongoing investor interest in space startups, bringing its total raised to $63.5 million. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding at a $1.6 billion valuation underscores the appetite for innovation in the sector.

themes.title: Defense Budget Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion to the space resilience line reflects a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space in national defense. This increase may signal a shift in priorities as the U.S. seeks to enhance its capabilities in an increasingly contested domain.
